# `parameter-serialization-changed`

Parameter style, explode, allowReserved or content changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `parameter-serialization-changed` (all locations), `query-parameter-serialization-changed`, `header-parameter-serialization-changed`, `cookie-parameter-serialization-changed`. Path parameters use `parameter-serialization-changed`. |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Parameters ([RULES.md section 4](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A parameter's `style`, `explode` or `allowReserved` changed, or it switched between `schema` and `content` or changed its `content` media type. Defaults are applied before comparing, so writing out a default isn't a change.

## Why this default

Clients encode the value the old way (e.g. `tags=a&tags=b` instead of `tags=a,b`), and the server misreads it.

## Example

From test case [`parameter-serialization-changed`](../../test/cases/parameter-serialization-changed/): explode changed from the default (true for form) to false.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
        - name: tags
          in: query
+         explode: false
          schema:
            type: array
```

Findings:

- `query-parameter-serialization-changed` · error · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  parameter-serialization-changed: error
```

## How to fix

Keep the old serialization, or add a new parameter with the new one.
